title: The Library
tagline: Thirty-six systems, a dozen sources, and one good copy of each game.
insertQuote: Sorted 12,043 games (about 857 GB) into one clean copy per game
what: My collection of classic games, kept on the home server and copied out to my handhelds and PC, with saves that move between them.
built: Sorted 12,043 games (about 857 GB) into one clean copy per game
Save syncing between the handhelds and the PC, with separate saves for each person
Automatic conversion of DS saves between the two formats emulators use, so a save made on one device loads on another
Tools that fill gaps in the collection and apply fan patches
credit: Built it: my scripts on top of Syncthing

making.problem: Games for 36 systems come in every format and from a dozen sources, half of them duplicates. Every handheld wants its own copy, and its own kind of save file.
how: One master library lives on the home server: one best copy of each game, with box art pulled for every system.
Syncthing carries the games and the saves out to each handheld and back.
A service on the server watches DS saves and writes the other emulator's format within about 15 seconds, keeps old versions, and backs it all up offsite that night.
